title: Automated QBRs and Tenant Synthetic Healthchecks Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Runbook and implementation guide for automating quarterly business reviews (QBRs) with tenant-level synthetic healthchecks and escalation triggers. Covers probe design, onboarding checklist, alert thresholds, automated report generation, and customer communication templates.
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines a production-ready approach to combine tenant-scoped synthetic healthchecks with automated QBR generation for enterprise customers. The goal is to surface service regressions early, quantify inference economics for customer stakeholders, and reduce manual effort for Customer Success (CS) and Support teams during QBR cadence or incident follow-ups.

Use cases:
- Ongoing tenant stability monitoring with SLA-aligned synthetic probes.
- Auto-generated QBR starter packs (latency/cost/quality metrics) for CS to curate.
- Early drift detection for model outputs and routing fallbacks.
- Customer-facing incident summaries synthesized from probe history.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Customer Success: owns QBR cadence, stakeholder invites, and narrative.
- Observability/Platform: maintains probe templates, probe scheduling service, and data exports.
- Support: triages alerts that cross severity thresholds and coordinates remediation.

High-level architecture:
1) Probe engine (service: telemetry-probes) runs tenant-scoped synthetic requests at configured frequencies.
2) Telemetry ingestion stores probe results in metrics DB (prometheus long-term + clickhouse for traces).
3) QBR generator (service: qbr-orchestrator) pulls aggregated metrics, runs evaluation suites (sample prompts/evals), and renders a QBR bundle (PDF + CSV + slide deck).
4) CS UI integration surfaces the latest QBR bundle in the account dashboard and creates a draft calendar invite.

Design principles for probes:
- Lightweight and deterministic: synthetic payloads should be small and reproducible across runs.
- Representative workload: each probe should map to a customer workload archetype (e.g., short-chat, long-context-generation, embedding-query).
- Isolated side-effects: probes must use a read-only instrumented model version or a dedicated probe model variant to avoid affecting production KV caches and billing.
- Per-tenant scoping: include tenant_id, routing tag, and pinned model version in probe metadata.

Probe catalog (recommended minimal set):
- latency-short: 100ms target P95, frequency: 1m, description: 16-token prompt generation.
- latency-long: 500ms target P95, frequency: 5m, description: 2048-token continuation sampling.
- embedding-query: frequency: 10m, description: 512-dim embedding for a canonical phrase.
- correctness-check: frequency: 30m, description: run eval on 10 curated prompts, compute pass-rate.
- kvcache-hit-rate: frequency: 5m, description: run prefix queries to estimate cache warmness.

Configuration table (example):
| probe_name | frequency | target_slo | sample_payload | model_variant | probe_account_role |
| latency-short | 1m | P95 < 120 ms | {"prompt": "Hello"} | pinned-v1 | probe-only-key |
| correctness-check | 30m | pass_rate >= 95% | 10-prompts.json | eval-pinned | probe-only-key |

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1. CS Owner creates the tenant probe profile in the Onboarding Hub with: tenant_id, contact list, pinned_model, preferred-region, business-hours window.
2. Platform provisions a probe-only API key scoped to tenant probe profile (TTL: 365d, rotation: automated quarterly).
3. Platform maps the tenant profile to the probe execution schedule and deploys probes into the tenant's routing group.
4. Run a 48-hour smoke window: validate probes produce results, check for false positives, and confirm cost estimate.
5. CS reviews the initial auto-QBR draft produced after 48 hours and adjusts which metrics are surfaced to stakeholders.
6. Mark onboarding complete once stabilization (no critical alerts) for 7 days is met.

Alerting and escalation matrix:
- Severity P0 (Immediate action): any probe indicating total unavailability for > 5 minutes across multiple model variants or region failover.
  - Trigger: probe engine stops receiving responses (HTTP 5xx or timeouts) across >=3 consecutive probes.
  - Notification: PagerDuty P0 to oncall SRE + CS lead + account executive.
  - Customer comms: immediate incident banner and dedicated Slack/phone bridge.

- Severity P1 (High): probe correctness-check pass_rate drops >= 10 percentage points below baseline OR P95 latency exceeds SLO for 30 minutes.
  - Trigger: rolling 30-minute window breach.
  - Notification: Support oncall, CS Owner, Platform engineer assigned.
  - Customer comms: templated email within 60 minutes and QBR note.

- Severity P2 (Medium): intermittent latency spikes or embedding variance above threshold affecting < 5% of probes.
  - Trigger: sporadic single-probe anomalies.
  - Notification: Support ticket auto-created, CS Owner notified next business day if unresolved.

Alert thresholds (recommended):
- Availability: <= 99.9% -> Severity P0 if outage confirmed.
- Latency: tenant P95 > configured_slo * 1.25 -> Severity P1 after 30m sustained.
- Correctness: pass_rate drop >= 10% absolute or sliding window drop >= 3% per 24h -> Severity P1.

Automated QBR generation templates and fields:
- QBR bundle includes: executive summary, availability & latency trends, inference economics, embedding stability, probed eval pass rates, incident timeline (last quarter), recommended actions, and appendix (raw CSVs, probe configs).
- Example CLI to generate a one-off bundle on demand:
  - curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood.local/qbr/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer PROBE_KEY" -d '{"tenant_id":"acct-123", "range":"90d", "include_evals": true}'
- Output: a zip with files: qbr-summary.pdf, metrics.csv, top-alerts.json, slide-deck.pptx.

Customer communication templates (short):
- Incident banner (templates/incident-banner.md):
  - Title: Service Degradation – [Short description]
  - Body: We are investigating increased latency affecting some requests for your account. Our engineers are working on a fix. We will post updates on this page and via your designated Slack channel.

- Post-incident summary (templates/post-incident-summary.md):
  - Title: Incident summary: [date] – [short title]
  - Sections: timeline, root cause, customer impact, mitigation steps taken, follow-up actions with ETA and owners.

False positives and calibration guidance:
- Initial two-week period: set probe sensitivity to conservative (wider thresholds) to avoid alert fatigue.
- Keep a rolling baseline window of 28 days for latency and correctness baselines.
- Label probes as diagnostic vs. business-critical; only business-critical probes trigger P1/P0 paths.

QBR cadence and automation schedule:
- Weekly: automated micro-report (1-page) emailed to CS Owner with rolling 7-day highlights.
- Monthly: draft QBR bundle auto-created and placed in CS draft folder for review.
- Quarterly: finalized QBR generated 7 days prior to customer meeting and attached to the calendar invite.

Sample metrics to include in QBR (minimum):
- Tenant availability (90d), error rate (4xx/5xx), P50/P95/P99 latency by route, per-token cost trends, embedding cosine drift, eval pass rates (trend), top 5 incidents with MTTR.

Operational playbook for escalations (numbered runbook):
1. Triage: Support receives alert -> create ticket with tags: tenant_id, probe_name, severity, link to recent probe traces.
2. Initial Diagnosis (15 min): Support verifies probe metadata and reproduces using probe-only-key. If reproduced, escalate to Platform engineer.
3. Mitigation (30-90 min): If mitigation is available (fallback to alternate model variant, restart worker pool, clear KV cache for that tenant), perform action and document steps.
4. Customer Communication (within 60 min for P1/P0): CS drafts and sends templated update; update incident banner.
5. Postmortem: For any P1/P0, create a postmortem within 72 hours and include probe history snippets and QBR implications.

Instrumentation and data retention:
- Probe raw payloads: retained 14 days.
- Aggregated metrics & rollups: retained 540 days for QBR trend analysis.
- Eval sample outputs (for correctness-check): stored in encrypted blob store with tenant access controls, retained 90 days by default.

Privacy and compliance notes:
- Probes must avoid sending any customer-sensitive real data. Use synthetic canonical text or pseudonymized samples.
- For regulated tenants requiring Private deployment, probes must run inside the tenant's VPC or with on-prem probe runner.

FAQ (short):
Q: Will synthetic probes increase my bill?
A: Probes are billed at a minimal rate and can be scoped to a probe-only billing key. We include an estimated monthly cost in the onboarding smoke window.

Q: Can a probe cause false cache warming?
A: Probes use probe-only model variants when possible. If probes must exercise the same model path as production, include metadata so KV cache metrics can be filtered out of customer billing.

Related pages and templates:
- Onboarding Hub -> Probe Profiles (internal link: /confluence/xxxxx)
- templates/post-incident-summary.md (internal templates repo)
- qbr-orchestrator README (github: internal/qbr-orchestrator)

Appendix: Example probe JSON (for latency-short)

  "probe_name": "latency-short",
  "tenant_id": "acct-123",
  "frequency": "60s",
  "payload": { "prompt": "Summarize: Redwood Inference" },

  "model_variant": "pinned-v1"
}
